section_summary: This section follows U.S. efforts in 1948–49 to establish occupation policy for civil aviation in Japan, including negotiations in the Far Eastern Commission and approval of a policy on Japanese participation, foreign airlines, internal service and airfields. It also covers British air service to Yokohama, requests for evidence about Japan’s aviation needs, and the opening pages of a research report on prewar Japanese civil aviation. Several SANACC papers and appendices appear twice in the section.

people.name: Daniel Noce
people.role: General, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army

people.name: Frank R. McCoy
people.role: U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission

people.name: George F. Kennan
people.role: Author of a policy report on Japan

people.name: Roswell H. Whitman
people.role: Acting Associate Chief, Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs; U.S. representative on FEC Committee 2

people.name: P. P. Claxton Jr.
people.role: State Department drafter or signatory of SANACC memorandum

subfiles.title: Letter on deferring the civil aviation policy paper
subfiles.about: Saltzman recommends postponing decisions on the civil aviation paper until broader Japan policy is reviewed.
subfiles.summary: Draper’s earlier views will be considered after Kennan’s report and Draper’s observations are assessed.

subfiles.title: British inquiry about yen earnings
subfiles.about: Ford asks whether British airlines may use locally earned yen to pay for services in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ford specifies passenger fares and freight charges as the earnings at issue.

subfiles.title: Reply on airline use of yen earnings
subfiles.about: Whitman explains that licensed foreign airlines should be able to spend yen earnings on local business expenses.
subfiles.summary: He cites SCAP licensing practice and says the draft currency clause was intended to permit such payments.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on draft SANACC civil aviation policy
subfiles.about: The memorandum examines Japanese flight restrictions, possible Soviet airline access and military airfield construction.
subfiles.summary: It recommends retaining the occupation ban on Japanese aviation and supporting controlled entry by foreign carriers, despite likely Army objections concerning Soviet flights. It also questions whether large military airfields, including Misawa, fit U.S. policy and urges clarification with the Army and Joint Chiefs of Staff.

subfiles.title: Despatch enclosing Japanese civil aviation monograph
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards a Japanese Foreign Office monograph advocating access to civil aviation.
subfiles.summary: The despatch finds its arguments insufficient to reconsider current or long term U.S. policy.

subfiles.title: Draft memorandum on civil aviation policy for SANACC
subfiles.about: A draft urges urgent SANACC consideration of a revised U.S. position for the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: It cites SCAP concurrence and three proposed appendices.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary, SANACC
subfiles.about: State seeks urgent approval of its revised policy for non-Japanese civil aviation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum cites SCAP’s concurrence and requests military review before FEC discussions resume.

subfiles.title: SANACC 379/2 circulation note
subfiles.about: The secretaries circulate the State member’s policy memorandum for urgent consideration.
subfiles.summary: Cover note for SANACC 379/2.

subfiles.title: SANACC 379/2 enclosure: State member’s memorandum
subfiles.about: State proposes adopting Appendix C as the U.S. position and negotiating it with FEC members.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure recounts SCAP and Far East Air Force concurrence, requests urgent clearance and suggests checking military objections. Pages 88 and 89 repeat much of the same opening text.

subfiles.title: SANACC 379/2 Appendix A: cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: State proposes FEC negotiations and language giving SCAP discretion over foreign civil aviation.
subfiles.summary: The cable rejects a proposed reciprocal-agreements test for excluding Soviet airlines as outside FEC competence. It proposes allowing foreign carriers when SCAP finds mutual trade, economic or cultural benefits, subject to security and facilities. State asks for SCAP’s views before September FEC discussions. The opening and middle passages appear on duplicate leaves.

subfiles.title: SANACC 379/2 Appendix B: SCAP reply
subfiles.about: SCAP states no objection to the proposed civil aviation policy.
subfiles.summary: The Far East Air Forces commander also concurs.

subfiles.title: SANACC 379/2 Appendix C: proposed U.S. policy
subfiles.about: The appendix sets proposed occupation rules for Japanese personnel, internal service, foreign carriers and aviation facilities.
subfiles.summary: It restricts Japanese flight operations, permits tightly controlled ground employment, and requires FEC consultation before internal civil service. SCAP may admit authorized foreign carriers subject to security, facilities and payment rules. The paper also regulates aerodromes and exempts official noncommercial flights; page 97 duplicates the opening of page 98.

subfiles.title: Revised page notice for SANACC 379/2
subfiles.about: The secretaries direct holders to replace page 34 of SANACC 379/2.
subfiles.summary: The revised page asks SANACC to determine whether the Joint Chiefs object.

subfiles.title: Airgram on cabotage in Japan
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State clarifies that granting cabotage rights remains subject to SANACC policy pending FEC action.
subfiles.summary: The airgram queries wording in despatch 570.

subfiles.title: Despatch on BOAC flying boat service to Yokohama
subfiles.about: Sebald forwards SCAP’s permission for BOAC to extend flying boat service to Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: He reports that Yokohama traffic will initially be limited to official mail and passengers.

subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum permitting BOAC’s Yokohama extension
subfiles.to: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: SCAP permits BOAC flying boats to use Yokohama under specified operating and support conditions.
subfiles.summary: Conditions cover visibility, navigation aids, harbor movement, moorings, radio contact, leased terminal huts and fuel. A request to discharge and pick up traffic remains under consideration.

subfiles.title: SANACC decision on policy for civil aviation in Japan
subfiles.about: SANACC approves Appendix C after the Joint Chiefs find no military objection.
subfiles.summary: The earlier SANACC 379/1 is removed from the agenda.

subfiles.title: Second copy of SANACC 379/2 circulation note
subfiles.about: A second copy circulates the State member’s policy memorandum for urgent consideration.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate SANACC 379/2 cover note.

subfiles.title: Second copy of SANACC 379/2 enclosure
subfiles.about: The enclosure again proposes Appendix C as the U.S. position for FEC negotiations.
subfiles.summary: It records SCAP concurrence and requests urgent military clearance. Pages 109 and 110 duplicate the opening; page 111 is a revised continuation.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Appendix A: cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: The repeated cable proposes a negotiated policy giving SCAP discretion over foreign airline entry.
subfiles.summary: State rejects an explicit reciprocal-agreements condition aimed at Soviet carriers and proposes a mutual-benefit finding instead. It requests SCAP’s response before FEC reconvenes. Pages 112–113, 114–115 and 116–117 contain repeated passages.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Appendix B: SCAP reply
subfiles.about: SCAP again reports no objection to the State proposal.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the reply at page 96.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Appendix C: proposed U.S. policy
subfiles.about: A second copy sets out proposed rules for non-Japanese civil aviation during the occupation.
subfiles.summary: It covers Japanese aviation employment, internal service, international carriers, cabotage, facilities and technical regulation. Page 121 contains visible revisions to the cabotage wording; pages 119 and 120 duplicate the opening.

subfiles.title: Second revised-page notice for SANACC 379/2
subfiles.about: The secretaries again instruct holders to replace page 34.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate replacement notice.

subfiles.title: Second copy of SANACC approval decision
subfiles.about: The notice records SANACC approval and the Joint Chiefs’ lack of military objection.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the decision at page 107.

subfiles.title: Instructions to U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Saltzman authorizes submission of the U.S. civil aviation position to the FEC.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed paper marks differences from FEC 245/18.

subfiles.title: U.S. position on non-Japanese civil aviation in Japan
subfiles.about: The paper presents the U.S. position on Japanese participation, internal service and foreign airline operations.
subfiles.summary: It allows SCAP limited discretion over Japanese flight operations and foreign carriers while referring internal service and cabotage to FEC procedures. Marked revisions concern cabotage, payment for Japanese services and consultation over technical regulations.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting SANACC 379/2 to Nanking
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: State sends SANACC 379/2 to the American Mission for information.
subfiles.summary: It follows an August 1947 instruction on civil aviation.

subfiles.title: Telegram approving Bharat Airways survey flight
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports approval of a Bharat Airways survey flight scheduled for 3 March 1949.
subfiles.summary: The Indian Liaison Mission was advised.

subfiles.title: Request for study of Japan’s civil aviation needs
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: State asks SCAP for evidence to support renewed FEC discussions of civil aviation policy.
subfiles.summary: The telegram requests an immediate study of economic justification, routes and international connections, including civil needs then met by military aviation. State also seeks arguments for allowing Japanese nationals to participate under SCAP control.

subfiles.title: Follow-up telegram requesting study completion date
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: State asks when SCAP will complete the civil aviation study requested on 21 April.
subfiles.summary: The timing matters to renewed FEC discussions.

subfiles.title: Tokyo reply on aviation study schedule
subfiles.about: Tokyo gives an expected date for its reply to State’s aviation study request.
subfiles.summary: A reply is expected around 10 June 1949.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on prewar aviation report
subfiles.about: Amrine seeks review of a historical report before possible distribution to FEC Committee No. 2.
subfiles.summary: The report is intended for members’ general information while policy discussions remain pending.

subfiles.title: Civil Aviation in the Japanese Economy, preliminary version
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Research for Far East
subfiles.about: The report surveys prewar Japanese air transport and estimates future domestic aviation needs.
subfiles.summary: It traces airline growth, government control and subsidies, then presents 1938 figures for routes, passengers, freight, mail and aircraft. It finds aviation’s measurable prewar contribution small compared with rail transport, while recognizing the value of speed and possible postwar relief for crowded transport systems. The report estimates that roughly 50 aircraft might serve Japan’s most urgent domestic routes. Page 145 begins a statistical table, and the report continues beyond this section.
